events.title: DEA places 4-fluoroamphetamine in Schedule I of Controlled Substances Act
events.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a final rule placing 4-fluoroamphetamine (4-FA), including its salts, isomers, and salts of isomers, in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, effective February 17, 2026. The action fulfills U.S. obligations under the 1971 UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances. DEA determined 4-FA has high potential for abuse, no currently accepted medical use in the United States, and lacks accepted safety for medical supervision. The rule imposes Schedule I regulatory controls, administrative, civil, and criminal sanctions on manufacture, distribution, import, export, research, and possession. DEA received nine public comments; two supported scheduling, five opposed it citing research concerns and potential therapeutic applications, and two were neutral.
events.why_relevant: Drug scheduling decisions restrict access to substances for research and medical purposes, affecting scientific inquiry, pharmaceutical development, and individual liberty regarding controlled substances.
